chunks: From him, from Ibrahim al-Kazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no harm in praying on the buriyah (a type of mat) and the khasafah (woven palm leaves), and on every plant, except the thamarah (fruit/leaves used for food)."

key_terms.اَلثَّمَرَةِ: Fruit or edible plant parts; in this context, it refers to a specific type of plant material used for food, which is excluded from the general permission.
key_terms.اَلْبُورِيَاءِ: A type of mat or carpet, often made from palm leaves or similar plant fibers.
key_terms.اَلْخَصَفَةِ: Woven mats made from palm leaves or reeds.

ai.seo_question: What materials are permissible for praying on according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This ruling from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of praying on plant-based mats, distinguishing between general vegetation and fruit-bearing plants. In Shia jurisprudence, the exclusion of *thamarah* (fruit) often relates to the principle of *istihlak* (consumption) or the potential for impurity if the fruit is eaten, whereas non-fruit plants like *buriyah* (palm fiber) and *khasafah* (woven reeds) are deemed pure and suitable for prostration.
